literal: Ruin is the great wealth of him who does not enjoy it himself, and who does not have the nature of giving even a single thing to the deserving.
translation: The immense wealth of a person who neither enjoys it himself nor has the nature of giving anything to those who deserve it is only a source of ruin.
modern: தான் அனுபவிக்காமலும், தகுதியுடையவர்களுக்கு ஒன்றையும் கொடுக்காத இயல்பு உடையவனுடைய பெரிய செல்வம் அவனுக்குக் குற்றத்தையே அல்லது அழிவையே தரும்.
explanation: This couplet highlights the useless and harmful nature of hoarded wealth. A person who possesses great wealth but does not use it for his own enjoyment, nor possesses the character to give even a small portion of it to deserving people, gains nothing from it. Instead, such unused and unshared wealth becomes a source of affliction or ruin ('ஏதம்') for him. The key words 'துவ்வான்' (one who does not enjoy) and 'ஈதல் இயல்பிலாதான்' (one who lacks the nature of giving) highlight the double failure of the miserly rich.
